title: Thiamethoxam-Induced Acute Methemoglobinemia in a Child.
authors: Shahid S, Abdulsalam TA, Ghafoor Zeyaei MA, Ben Mechlia N.
tables: Vital signs during hospital course  Vital signs recorded during the hospital stay showed initial tachycardia, elevated respiratory rate, and persistent hypoxia despite oxygen support, followed by clinical stabilization.  bpm: breaths per minute, rpm: respiration per minute, NRB: non-rebreather mask.

Capillary blood gas and methemoglobin trend  Serial capillary blood gas results and MetHb levels demonstrated rapid biochemical improvement and resolution of methemoglobinemia following methylene blue administration.
